exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Vertically Stretched Sine or Cosine Function

question.explanation:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y=\cos x.$

  • Then, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $\dfrac 1 2.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is $y=\dfrac 1 2$

Method 2

We know that that $y = \cos{x}$ has a maximum value of $1.$

\[ \cos{x} \leq 1 \]

Multiplying both sides of the above inequality by $\dfrac{1}{2}$ gives:

\begin{align*} \dfrac 1 2\cdot\cos{x} & \leq \dfrac1 2\cdot 1\\[3pt] \dfrac 1 2\cos{x} &\leq \dfrac 1 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the maximum value of $\dfrac 1 2\cos{x}$ is $\dfrac 1 2.$

question.explanation:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \cos{x}.$

  • Then, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $\dfrac{5}{2}.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is $y = \dfrac{5}{2}.$

Method 2

We know that that $y = \cos{x}$ has a maximum value of $1.$ \[ \cos{x} \leq 1 \]

Multiplying both sides of the above inequality by $\dfrac{5}{2}$ gives \begin{align*} \dfrac{5}{2} \cdot \cos{x} & \leq \dfrac{5}{2} \cdot 1\\[5pt] \dfrac{5}{2}\cos{x} & \leq \dfrac{5}{2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the maximum value of $\dfrac{5}{2}\cos{x}$ is $\dfrac{5}{2}.$

exampleAnswers.title: Determining the Amplitude Given the Equation of a Vertically Stretched Sine or Cosine Function

question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y = \sin{x}.$

  • Then, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $\dfrac{5}{2}.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is $y_\max = \dfrac{5}{2}$ and the minimum value is $y_\min = -\dfrac{5}{2}.$ Therefore, the amplitude is \begin{align*} \textrm{Amplitude } &=\dfrac{y_\max - y_\min}{2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{5}{2} - \left(-\dfrac{5}{2}\right)\right)}{2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{5}{2}\right)}{2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{5}{2}. \end{align*}

question.explanation:
To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of $y=\cos x.$

  • Then, stretch it parallel to the $y$-axis by a stretch factor of $4.$

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the maximum value is $y_\max=4$ and the minimum value is $y_\min=-4.$ Therefore, the amplitude is:

\begin{align*} \textrm{Amplitude } &=\dfrac{y_\max - y_\min}2\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4 - (-4)}2\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4+4}2\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8}2\\[5pt] &= 4 \end{align*}
